items.title: 2.4 Derivatives of Inverse Trigonometric Functions (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 38-40: formulas (i)-(vi), Proof (1) sin^-1, Proof (2) cot^-1, Proof (3) sec^-1, Challenge! and Recall! boxes, Example 6

blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum bachon! Pichle sabaq mein humne sin, cos, tan waghera ke derivatives nikale. Aaj un ke ulte (inverse) functions ki baari hai: \(\sin^{-1} x\), \(\cos^{-1} x\) waghera. \(\sin^{-1} x\) ka matlab hai 'woh angle jis ka sine \(x\) ho'. Maslan \(\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\pi}{6}\). Dilchasp baat yeh hai ke in ke derivatives mein koi trigonometric function nahin bachta, sirf algebra rehti hai. Aur in ko saabit karne ke liye hum wohi implicit differentiation use karenge jo abhi 2.3.3 mein seekhi.

Kitab kehti hai: hum yeh saabit karenge:
(i)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin^{-1} x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}\]
jab \(x \in (-1, 1)\)
(ii)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\cos^{-1} x) = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}\]
jab \(x \in (-1, 1)\)
(iii)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\tan^{-1} x) = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}\]
jab \(x \in \mathbb{R}\)
(iv)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\cot^{-1} x) = -\dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}\]
jab \(x \in \mathbb{R}\)
(v)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sec^{-1} x) = \dfrac{1}{|x|\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}}\]
jab \(x \in (-\infty, -1) \cup (1, \infty)\)
(vi)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\csc^{-1} x) = -\dfrac{1}{|x|\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}}\]
jab \(x \in (-\infty, -1) \cup (1, \infty)\)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh ehtiyat kyun maangte hain? Inverse trigonometric function, jaise \(\sin^{-1} x\), sirf ek principal range (asal hadd) mein define hota hai, taa ke har input ka sirf ek output ho aur yeh sach mein function ho. Neeche ke har saboot mein yahi range batati hai ke square root ka sign plus lena hai ya minus.
Ek aasan pattern: teen "co" wale formulas (ii), (iv), (vi) bilkul (i), (iii), (v) jaise hain, bas aage minus laga hai. Yaani sirf teen formulas yaad karne hain, baqi teen muft.

blocks.caption: Sabooton mein istemal hone wale domains aur principal ranges (hamari table)

blocks.text: Proof (1)

Maan lijiye \(y = \sin^{-1}(x)\), jahan \(x \in [-1, 1]\) aur \(y \in \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\).
\[\sin y = x \quad \ldots(1)\]
Equation (1) ko \(x\) ke lihaaz se differentiate karne par
\[\cos y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{\cos y} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\cos^{2} y}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \sin^{2} y}}\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin^{-1} x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}\]
jab \(x \in (-1, 1)\) \((\because \sin y = x)\)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Har saboot ka tareeqa ek hi hai, teen qadam: inverse function ko aam trigonometric equation bana do (\(y = \sin^{-1} x\) ka matlab \(\sin y = x\)), phir implicit differentiation karo (2.3.3), aur aakhir mein jawab ko wapas \(x\) mein badal do.
\(\cos y = +\sqrt{1 - \sin^{2} y}\) kyun, minus kyun nahin? Kyun ke \(y\) range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hai, aur wahan cosine kabhi negative nahin hota (pehla aur chautha quadrant). Is liye positive root hi sahi hai.
\(x \ne \pm 1\) kyun? Wahan \(\cos y = 0\) hota hai aur zero se divide nahin kar sakte. Graph ke lihaaz se, \(\sin^{-1} x\) ke graph ke dono kinaron par tangent khari (vertical) hoti hai, jis ka slope define nahin.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(x = 0\) par \(\sin^{-1} x\) ka slope kya hai? Formula se \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - 0}} = 1\). Aur \(x = 0.99\) par? \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - 0.9801}} \approx 7.09\). Kinaare ki taraf graph kitna tez ho jata hai!
Proof (2)

Maan lijiye \(y = \cot^{-1}(x)\), jahan \(y \in (0, \pi)\) aur \(x \in \mathbb{R}\).
\[\cot y = x \quad \ldots(2)\]
Ab equation (2) ko \(x\) ke lihaaz se differentiate karte hain:
\[-\csc^{2} y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1\]
\(\left((\cot y)' = -\csc^{2} y\right)\)
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{1}{\csc^{2} y}\]
\((\csc y \ne 0, \ y \in (0, \pi) \text{ ke liye})\)
\[= -\dfrac{1}{1 + \cot^{2} y}\]
\((\because 1 + \cot^{2} y = \csc^{2} y)\)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\cot^{-1} x) = -\dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}\]
har \(x \in \mathbb{R}\) ke liye \((\because \cot y = x)\)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab Proof (2) mein \(\cot y = x\) ko equation (2) ka number deti hai, lekin agli line mein likhti hai 'We differentiate equation (1)'. Sahi yeh hai ke equation (2) (yani \(\cot y = x\)) ko differentiate karte hain; upar humne sahi likha hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ek uljhan door kar lein: kitab sabooton ko 1, 2, 3 number deti hai, lekin formulas (i) se (vi) tak hain. Proof (2) asal mein formula (iv), \(\cot^{-1} x\), ka saboot hai, aur Proof (3) formula (v), \(\sec^{-1} x\), ka.
Is saboot mein sign ka koi masla nahin: \(\csc^{2} y = 1 + \cot^{2} y\) mein koi square root nahin aata, is liye formula har real \(x\) ke liye sahi hai. \(\csc^{2} y\) kabhi zero nahin hota, is liye divide karna jaiz hai.
Proof (3)

Maan lijiye \(y = \sec^{-1} x\), jahan \(x \in (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\) aur \(y \in [0, \pi] - \left\{\frac{\pi}{2}\right\}\)
\[\sec y = x \quad \ldots(1), \quad |x| \ge 1\]
Equation (1) ko \(x\) ke lihaaz se differentiate karte hain:
\[\sec y\tan y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1\]
\(\left(\because (\sec y)' = \sec y\tan y\right)\)
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{\sec y\tan y}\]
jahan \(\sec y \ne 0\) aur \(\tan y \ne 0\)
\(\tan y \ne 0 \Rightarrow y \ne 0\) aur \(y \ne \pi \Rightarrow x \ne -1, 1\), aur equation (1) se:
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{x\tan y} \quad \ldots(2)\]
\((\because \sec y = x)\)
\[\tan y = \begin{cases}\sqrt{\tan^{2} y}, & y \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \\ -\sqrt{\tan^{2} y}, & y \in \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)\end{cases}\]
\[= \begin{cases}\sqrt{\sec^{2} y - 1}, & y \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \\ -\sqrt{\sec^{2} y - 1}, & y \in \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)\end{cases}\]
\[\tan y = \begin{cases}\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}, & x \in (1, \infty) \\ -\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}, & x \in (-\infty, -1)\end{cases}\]

Ab tak ka natija (sahi intervals ke saath) dobara:
\[\tan y = \begin{cases}\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}, & x \in (1, \infty) \\ -\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}, & x \in (-\infty, -1)\end{cases}\]
kyun ke \(\sec y = x\), aur jab \(y \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) ho to \(x \in (1, \infty)\), jab ke \(y \in \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)\) ho to \(x \in (-\infty, -1)\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab \(\tan y\) ko pehle sahi likhti hai, phir dobara likhte waqt intervals ghalat chhap deti hai: \(x \in (1, -1)\) aur \(x \in (-\infty, 1)\). \((1, -1)\) to koi interval hi nahin banta. Sahi intervals \((1, \infty)\) aur \((-\infty, -1)\) hain, jaise pichli line mein aur kitab ki apni wajah (reason) mein likha hai.

\(\tan y\) ki value equation (2) mein rakhein:
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}}, & x \in (1, \infty) \\[2mm] \dfrac{1}{-x\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}}, & x \in (-\infty, -1)\end{cases}\]
Is tarah,
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sec^{-1} x) = \dfrac{1}{|x|\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}}\]
jahan \(x \in (-\infty, -1) \cup (1, \infty)\) \(\left(\because |x| = \begin{cases}x & \text{agar } x \ge 0 \\ -x & \text{agar } x < 0\end{cases}\right)\)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Do cases kyun bane? \(\tan y = \pm\sqrt{\sec^{2} y - 1}\), aur sign quadrant par depend karta hai. Jab \(y \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) (pehla quadrant), to \(x = \sec y > 1\) aur \(\tan y > 0\). Jab \(y \in \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)\) (doosra quadrant), to \(x = \sec y < -1\) aur \(\tan y < 0\).
Kamaal ki baat: dono soorton mein \(x\tan y\) positive hai aur \(|x|\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}\) ke barabar hai. \(x > 1\) par yeh \(x\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}\) hai, aur \(x < -1\) par \((-x)\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}\) (do negative mil kar positive). Isi liye formula mein \(|x|\) aata hai. Is ka matlab yeh bhi hai ke \(\sec^{-1} x\) ka graph har jagah barhta (increasing) hai.

blocks.title: Challenge!
blocks.text: Formulas (2), (3) aur (6) saabit kijiye.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ka Challenge kehta hai 'Prove formulae (2), (3) and (5)'. Lekin formula (5), yani (v), upar Proof (3) mein pehle hi saabit ho chuka hai. Jo formulas abhi baqi hain woh (ii), (iii) aur (vi) hain, is liye ghaliban (5) ki jagah (6) hona chahiye. Upar humne (6) likha hai.

blocks.title: Recall!
blocks.text: \[\sqrt{x^{2}} = \begin{cases}x, & \text{agar } x \ge 0 \\ -x, & \text{agar } x < 0\end{cases}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Challenge ke liye rehnumai (wohi teen qadam wala tareeqa). Pehle khud koshish kijiye, phir yahan milaiye:
(ii) \(y = \cos^{-1} x\), \(y \in [0, \pi]\): \(\cos y = x\), is liye \(-\sin y\frac{dy}{dx} = 1\). \([0, \pi]\) mein sine kabhi negative nahin, is liye \(\sin y = \sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\), aur \(\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}\), \(x \in (-1, 1)\).
(iii) \(y = \tan^{-1} x\), \(y \in \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\): \(\tan y = x\), is liye \(\sec^{2} y\frac{dy}{dx} = 1\), aur identity \(\sec^{2} y = 1 + \tan^{2} y\) se \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{1 + x^{2}}\). Yahan bhi koi root nahin, is liye har real \(x\) ke liye.
(vi) \(y = \csc^{-1} x\), \(y \in \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right] - \{0\}\): \(\csc y = x\), is liye \(-\csc y\cot y\frac{dy}{dx} = 1\), yani \(\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{1}{x\cot y}\). \(x > 1\) par \(\cot y = \sqrt{x^{2} - 1}\) aur \(x < -1\) par \(\cot y = -\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}\). Dono soorton mein \(x\cot y = |x|\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}\), is liye \(\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}}\).

blocks.title: Example 6
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = x\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{a}\right) - \sqrt{a^{2} - x^{2}}\). Kitab ka hal chupke se \(a > 0\) aur \(|x| < a\) maan leta hai.
Maloom karna: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: pehla term \(x\) aur \(\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)\) ka zarb hai, is liye product rule; saath formula (ii) aur chain rule. Doosra term square root hai, is liye power rule aur chain rule.

Step 1: x ke lihaaz se differentiate karein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)\]
\[\quad + x\left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - (x/a)^{2}}} \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)\right)\]
\[\quad - \dfrac{1}{2}(a^{2} - x^{2})^{-1/2} \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}(a^{2} - x^{2})\]
Kyun: \(x \cdot \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)\) par product rule (\(x\) ka derivative 1). \(\frac{d}{dx}\cos^{-1} u = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\frac{du}{dx}\), jahan \(u = \frac{x}{a}\). Aur \(\sqrt{a^{2} - x^{2}} = (a^{2} - x^{2})^{1/2}\), is liye power rule se \(\frac{1}{2}(\ldots)^{-1/2}\).

Step 2: Andar wale derivatives nikalein
\[= \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right) - \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{\frac{a^{2} - x^{2}}{a^{2}}}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{a}\]
\[\quad - \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a^{2} - x^{2}}}(-2x)\]
Kyun: \(\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x}{a}\right) = \frac{1}{a}\) (\(a\) constant hai), \(\frac{d}{dx}(a^{2} - x^{2}) = -2x\), aur \(1 - \frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} = \frac{a^{2} - x^{2}}{a^{2}}\) (common denominator).

Step 3: Simplify karein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right) - \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{a^{2} - x^{2}}}\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{a^{2} - x^{2}}}\]
\[= \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)\]
Kyun: \(a > 0\) ke liye \(\sqrt{\frac{a^{2} - x^{2}}{a^{2}}} = \frac{\sqrt{a^{2} - x^{2}}}{a}\). Is liye doosra term \(\frac{x \cdot a}{\sqrt{a^{2} - x^{2}}} \cdot \frac{1}{a} = \frac{x}{\sqrt{a^{2} - x^{2}}}\) ban gaya. Teesre term mein \(-\frac{1}{2} \cdot (-2x) = +x\). Aakhri do terms barabar aur ulte sign wale hain, is liye cancel ho gaye.
Dhyan dein: itna lamba function, aur jawab itna chhota! Exam mein aise sawal mein aakhir mein cancellation ki umeed rakhiye.
Tasdeeq: \(a = 2\), \(x = 1\) lein. Jawab \(\cos^{-1}\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\pi}{3} \approx 1.0472\) deta hai. Calculator se \(\frac{y(1.001) - y(0.999)}{0.002} \approx 1.0472\). Dono barabar.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 6 mein \(\sqrt{a^{2}} = a\) liya gaya hai, yani \(a > 0\) maana gaya hai (aur \(|x| < a\), taa ke square root real rahe). Agar \(a < 0\) hota to \(\sqrt{a^{2}} = -a\) hota aur aakhri do terms cancel na hote. Kitab yeh shart nahin likhti, lekin exam mein ek line mein likh dena achi baat hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(a) \(\frac{d}{dx}\sin^{-1}(2x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - (2x)^{2}}} \cdot 2 = \frac{2}{\sqrt{1 - 4x^{2}}}\), jab \(|x| < \frac{1}{2}\). Yahan andar \(2x\) hai, is liye chain rule se 2 ka factor aaya.
(b) \(\frac{d}{dx}\tan^{-1}(x^{2}) = \frac{1}{1 + (x^{2})^{2}} \cdot 2x = \frac{2x}{1 + x^{4}}\). Andar \(x^{2}\), us ka derivative \(2x\).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \((\sin^{-1} x)' = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}\), \((\tan^{-1} x)' = \frac{1}{1 + x^{2}}\), \((\sec^{-1} x)' = \frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}}\); 'co' wale teen in hi ke minus wale roop hain.
2. Saboot ka tareeqa: inverse ko trigonometric equation banao, implicitly differentiate karo, wapas \(x\) mein badlo.
3. Principal range har square root ka sign tay karti hai; isi liye (v) aur (vi) mein \(|x|\) aata hai.
4. Chain ke saath: \(\frac{d}{dx}\sin^{-1} u = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\frac{du}{dx}\), baqi bhi isi tarah.
5. Kitab ki teen ghaltiyan is sabaq mein: Proof (2) mein equation ka number, Proof (3) mein intervals, aur Challenge mein (5) ki jagah (6).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\sin^{-1} x\) ko \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\) samajh lena: yahan \(-1\) ka matlab inverse function hai, reciprocal nahin.
2. \((\sec^{-1} x)'\) ke liye \(\frac{1}{x\sqrt{x^{2} - 1}}\) likhna: \(|x|\) ke baghair \(x < -1\) par sign ghalat ho jata hai.
3. Chain rule ka factor bhool jana, jaise \(\frac{d}{dx}\sin^{-1}(2x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - 4x^{2}}}\) (2 ghaib).
4. \(x = \pm 1\) par formulas lagana, jahan (i), (ii), (v), (vi) define hi nahin.
